mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for four consecutive weeks (-16.6 to -36.6). This momentum reflects compounding behavioral inertia: each week of lower retail activity reinforces habits (online shopping, reduced errands) that persist, so the downward trend continues into the next four weeks without any new trigger.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -16.6 to -36.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, indicating the decline trend reversed rather than continued.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility partially recovered from -50.0 to -29.4 over two weeks, suggesting restriction easing is underway. If WORKPLACES crosses back above the -30 threshold for two consecutive weeks, commuter-linked retail footfall (lunch, shopping on the way home) should rebound, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -30 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES recovered from -50.0 at t-2w to -29.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat even after WORKPLACES sustains levels above -30 for two weeks, falsifying the commuter-linked rebound mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES jointly proxy commuting intensity. When both series rise together (indicating synchronized return to office-based routines), the combined effect on incidental retail visits is larger than either series alone, producing a compounding positive effect on RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show partial recovery from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise even when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase simultaneously over consecutive weeks, falsifying the joint-commuting interaction mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The Northern Beaches cluster restrictions imposed in late December 2020 remain partly in force, as shown by RESIDENTIAL mobility staying elevated (+15 to +20) and RETAIL_REC continuing to fall. Under a tightening-restriction regime, stay-at-home orders suppress retail visits further over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 8.4 to 15.7 while RETAIL_REC fell from -16.6 to -36.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated, indicating restrictions are not the binding constraint.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained elevation of RESIDENTIAL mobility above +15 for two consecutive weeks signals heightened household risk-aversion. This behavioral caution substitutes retail trips with home-based consumption (delivery, online shopping), suppressing RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +15 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 14.3 at t-1w and 15.7 at t-0w, both above 15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +15 for two weeks, indicating no substitution effect from home-based behavior.

mechanism_narrative: January in Sydney is peak summer holiday season; despite restriction-driven declines, seasonal leisure demand (beach trips, outdoor dining, shopping during school holidays) typically counteracts suppression, producing a rebound in both PARKS and RETAIL_REC as households resume holiday-related outings over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-01-15 falls within Australian summer school holidays
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and PARKS both continue to decline through the holiday period, indicating seasonal leisure demand did not offset restriction effects.

mechanism_narrative: Large week-on-week swings in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES (e.g., WORKPLACES jumped from -50.0 to -34.3 to -29.4) indicate volatile, transitional mobility conditions. When TRANSIT changes by more than 10 points week-on-week alongside WORKPLACES recovery, short-term mean reversion in RETAIL_REC follows within one week as commuters resume incidental shopping.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change exceeds 10 points in magnitude
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -28.3 to -49.3 to -42.3 to -46.0 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no short-term uptick within one week following a TRANSIT swing exceeding 10 points, falsifying the volatility-driven rebound mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stayed far less negative than RETAIL_REC (-9.0 vs -36.6), indicating the public is restricting trips to essential-only categories under ongoing restrictions. This essential-only substitution pattern should persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed relative to GROCERY_PHARM over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near -9.0 while RETAIL_REC fell to -36.6
failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC narrows substantially (RETAIL_REC rising toward GROCERY_PHARM levels) within four weeks, indicating essential-only substitution is not driving the suppression.
